questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution deals with the formation of a new State?
questions.explanation: Article 3 deals with the formation of a new State.

questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic of the Panchayati Raj system in West Bengal?
questions.explanation: The Panchayati Raj system in West Bengal is a 3-Tier system.

questions.question: Who is the head of the West Bengal Legislative Assembly?
questions.explanation: The Speaker is the head of the West Bengal Legislative Assembly.

questions.question: Which of the following is a fundamental duty under the Indian Constitution?
questions.explanation: Respecting the national flag is a fundamental duty under the Indian Constitution.

questions.question: What is the term of office for a Member of the Legislative Assembly in West Bengal?
questions.explanation: The term of office for a Member of the Legislative Assembly in West Bengal is 5 years.

questions.question: The Ganges-Brahmaputra river system, which is the lifeline of West Bengal, originates from which place?
questions.explanation: The river system originates from the Himalayas.

questions.question: Which of the following districts in West Bengal is the largest in terms of area?
questions.explanation: Murshidabad is the largest district in West Bengal.

questions.question: The Sundarbans, the largest mangrove forest in the world, is located in which part of West Bengal?
options: The northern part of the state
The eastern part of the state
The southern part of the state
The western part of the state
questions.explanation: The Sundarbans is located in the southern part of West Bengal.

questions.question: Which mountain range runs along the northern part of West Bengal?
questions.explanation: The Himalayas run along the northern part of West Bengal.

questions.question: Which of the following rivers flows through the Dooars region of West Bengal?
questions.explanation: The Teesta flows through the Dooars region of West Bengal.

questions.question: Which of the following schemes has been recently launched by the Government of West Bengal to promote entrepreneurship among women?
questions.explanation: Launched in 2026 to empower women through entrepreneurship.

questions.question: The West Bengal government has recently signed an MoU with which of the following countries to boost trade and investment?
questions.explanation: To enhance bilateral trade and investment opportunities.

questions.question: The West Bengal government has recently launched a new initiative to provide financial assistance to the farmers affected by the recent floods in the state. What is the name of this initiative?
questions.explanation: Launched in 2026 to provide financial assistance to farmers.

questions.question: The West Bengal government has recently decided to launch a new scheme to promote the use of electric vehicles in the state. What is the name of this scheme?
questions.explanation: To promote the use of electric vehicles in the state.

questions.question: The West Bengal government has recently decided to observe which of the following days as a State Level Holiday?
questions.explanation: To commemorate the State Foundation Day.

questions.question: A shopkeeper in Kolkata sells an article at Rs. 480, after offering a discount of 15%. Find the marked price of the article.
questions.explanation: Marked price is the original price before discount.

questions.question: A person invested Rs. 12,000 in a business and earned a profit of 20%. What is the person's share of profit?
questions.explanation: Profit is calculated on the investment amount.

questions.question: A person buys 5 kilograms of potatoes at Rs. 20 per kilogram and sells 5 kilograms at Rs. 25 per kilogram. What is his profit percentage?
questions.explanation: Profit percentage is calculated on the selling price and cost price.

questions.question: A shopkeeper in Howrah buys an article at Rs. 240 and sells it at a profit of 25%. How much money does he make from this sale?
questions.explanation: Profit is the difference between selling price and cost price.

questions.question: A person buys a share at Rs. 96 and sells it at Rs. 144. What is the percentage increase in the value of the share?
questions.explanation: Percentage increase is calculated on the original value.

questions.question: A water pump fills 2/3 of a tank in 6 hours. How long will it take to fill the tank completely?
questions.explanation: The pump fills 2/3 of the tank in 6 hours, so it will fill the whole tank in the same time.

questions.question: If 4 men can dig 24 metres of canal in 8 hours, how much distance will 8 men dig in 6 hours?
questions.explanation: The work done by 4 men in 8 hours is 24 metres, so the work done by 8 men in 6 hours is proportionally 2 times the work done in 8 hours.

questions.question: A pipe can fill 2/5 of a tank in 1 hour. Another pipe can fill 1/4 of the tank in 1 hour. How long will it take to fill the tank completely if both pipes are opened together?
questions.explanation: The combined rate of filling the tank is the sum of the individual rates, which is (2/5 + 1/4) = 9/20 of the tank per hour.

questions.question: A well with a capacity of 2400 m3 can be filled by 8 pipes in 10 hours. How many hours will it take to fill the well by 4 pipes?
questions.explanation: The work done by 8 pipes in 10 hours is 2400 m3, so the work done by 4 pipes in 1 hour is 1/2 of the work done by 8 pipes in 1 hour.

questions.question: A tank can be filled by a pipe in 12 hours. Due to a leakage, it takes 18 hours to fill the tank. The leakage can be stopped by closing a valve in 4 hours. How long will it take to fill the tank in the absence of the valve?
questions.explanation: The effective rate of filling the tank is the rate of the pipe minus the rate of the leakage, which is 1/12 - 1/18 = 1/36 of the tank per hour.

questions.question: A car covers a distance of 240 km in 4 hours. What is its speed?
questions.explanation: Speed is calculated as total distance divided by total time.

questions.question: A bus travels from Kolkata to Siliguri at an average speed of 40 km/h. If the distance between the two cities is 250 km, how many hours will it take?
questions.explanation: Time taken is calculated as distance divided by speed.

questions.question: A man covers a certain distance in 6 hours. If he covers half of this distance in 3 hours, what is his speed?
questions.explanation: Since the man covers half the distance in 3 hours, his speed for this distance is 60 km/h.

questions.question: A train travels from Howrah to Bardhaman at an average speed of 80 km/h. If the distance between the two stations is 100 km, how many hours will it take?
questions.explanation: Time taken is calculated as distance divided by speed.

questions.question: A car travels from Jalpaiguri to Alipurduar at an average speed of 60 km/h. If the distance between the two cities is 180 km, how many hours will it take?
questions.explanation: Time taken is calculated as distance divided by speed.

questions.question: A man is called father of his son's mother, but not grandfather of his son. How is the man related to the son?
questions.explanation: He is the son of the son's mother.

questions.question: A family has three generations. Grandfather X has three children: Y, Z and W. Y has a son P. Z has a daughter Q. W has a son R. Who is the father of Q?
questions.explanation: Z is the father of Q.

questions.question: A, B, C, D, E and F are six people. A is the brother of B. C is the sister of D and E. E is the sister of F. Who is the brother of F?
questions.explanation: E is the brother of F.

questions.question: In a family, there are five members: A, B, C, D and E. A is the daughter of B and C, but not the daughter of D and E. A is the sister of D and E. Who is the father of A?
questions.explanation: B is the father of A.

questions.question: A man introduces his son as 'my sons only son'. How is the man related to the son?
questions.explanation: The man is the father of the son.

questions.question: If a person walks 8 km east from a place and then 3 km towards north, then which direction is he from the starting place?
questions.explanation: Use of Pythagoras theorem is required.

questions.question: A person is facing north direction. He turns 135 degrees to his right. Which direction is he facing now?
questions.explanation: Use of clockwise rotation is required.

questions.question: A person is standing at a place. He walks 15 km from that place to a river. He then turns right and walks 10 km. Then he turns right and walks 6 km. Which direction is the river from the place?
questions.explanation: Use of clockwise rotation is required.

questions.question: A boy is facing the morning sun. If he turns 90 degrees to his left, which direction is he facing?
questions.explanation: Use of clockwise rotation is required.

questions.question: A person is standing at a place. He walks 5 km east and reaches a hill. Then he turns left and walks 6 km. Which direction is the hill from the starting place?
questions.explanation: Use of Pythagoras theorem is required.
